title: SCOPE: Cost-Efficient Model Selection for Compound AI Systems under Quality Constraints

problem.claim: Select an LLM for each module of a compound AI system to minimize average system cost while satisfying a user-specified overall quality threshold.

gap.claim: Using a single expensive LLM across all modules can impose prohibitive costs at scale, while existing approaches rely on expensive dataset-level evaluations.

contributions.claim: Formalizes constrained LLM selection for compound AI systems using differences in LLM pricing and capabilities.

Proposes SCOPE, a cost-efficient optimization algorithm that uses per-query results to estimate system cost and quality, constructs confidence bounds, and guides the search for promising LLM combinations.
Offers theoretical assurances that the required quality threshold is met while average cost remains near optimal.

stated_novelty.claim: SCOPE is presented as a cost-efficient optimization algorithm that differs from existing approaches by exploiting per-query results instead of relying on expensive dataset-level evaluations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Against 7 baselines on three data processing tasks, SCOPE is reported to outperform all baselines.
Under the same search budget and quality constraint, SCOPE is reported to find solutions with up to 20× lower cost than the best competitor during the search.
SCOPE is reported to achieve up to 6× lower final cost in the returned solution.

narrative_sequence.summary: Compound AI systems use multiple LLM modules for complex, multi-step tasks beyond a single model's capabilities.
Single expensive LLMs improve whole-system quality but create prohibitive costs at scale.
The work formulates constrained per-module LLM selection to minimize average cost while meeting a quality threshold.
SCOPE uses per-query estimates and confidence bounds to search efficiently over LLM combinations and provides theoretical guarantees.
The abstract reports comparisons with 7 baselines on three data processing tasks and lower search and final costs under stated constraints.

source_observation.claim: The reported cost improvements are evaluated under the same search budget and quality constraint.

interpretation.claim: Cost comparisons depend on holding search budget and quality requirements fixed.

application.claim: Compare cost-efficient selection methods under matched search budgets and quality constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported improvements generalize beyond the three evaluated data processing tasks.

unknowns: The specific LLMs, module architectures, datasets, and task details are not provided.
The quality metric, threshold-setting procedure, search budget, and evaluation protocol are not specified.
The theoretical assumptions and forms of the guarantees are not described.
The statistical uncertainty, computational overhead, and failure cases of SCOPE are not reported.
